subject.title: [Feature]: Network Access Control (allowedDomains / denyDomains) — Egress Firewall

question: What should own OpenClaw's public web-tool egress boundary: a scoped `web_fetch` policy, a cross-tool search/fetch/browser policy, or managed-proxy-owned egress?
rationale: This is a public security/config surface that users will treat as an exfiltration boundary, and the currently open implementation directions choose different guarantees.

options.title: Sponsor Scoped web_fetch First
options.body: Use the narrow hostname-allowlist PR direction as the first contract while leaving denied domains, managed search, browser, and proxy behavior as explicit follow-up work.

options.title: Design Shared Egress Policy
options.body: Pause narrow knobs until maintainers define one cross-tool policy for fetch, search, browser, providers, redirects, caches, and proxy routing.

options.title: Delegate To Managed Proxy
options.body: Make `proxy.enabled` plus external operator policy the supported egress boundary instead of adding local domain firewall knobs to web tools.

recommendation.title: Sponsor Scoped web_fetch First
recommendation.body: Use the narrow hostname-allowlist PR direction as the first contract while leaving denied domains, managed search, browser, and proxy behavior as explicit follow-up work.

likelyOwner.reason: Peter Steinberger has the strongest feature-history connection to the SSRF guard and hostname allowlist primitive that any native policy would extend.
